data.name: Marmaduke
data.long_meaning: From the Old English words 'marm' (sea) and 'duc' (ruler), Marmaduke was a popular name for brave knights in medieval England. In Christian lore, Marmaduke is also associated with St. Marmaduke, a 13th-century Scottish saint.

data.cultural_impact: Marmaduke is an interesting name that carries a rich cultural heritage, originating from the Old English words 'marm' (sea) and 'duc' (ruler). In medieval England, this name was given to brave knights, reflecting their strength and power over the sea. It also suggests a connection to the coastal regions and the maritime community.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian lore, Marmaduke is also associated with St. Marmaduke, a 13th-century Scottish saint who is said to have given his life in defense of the faith. The name carries spiritual significance as a reminder of courage, devotion, and resistance in the face of adversity. St. Marmaduke's life story can inspire us to be strong in our beliefs and unwavering in our commitment to God, even in the midst of difficult circumstances.
